subject: Post-call: Acme TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Acme TCO recap & next steps

John,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can get you a clean TCO to take to procurement. If I missed anything, please flag.

Summary of pain / goals discussed:
- Primary pain: per-request token cost is unpredictable at scale and spikes during peak chat bursts; team needs a predictable monthly cost to fit into a fixed budget.
- Secondary: tail latency (p95) during concurrent sessions is impacting UX for high-value workflows.
- Compliance: you need audit logs and regionally isolated deployments for sensitive customer PII.

What we covered that helps with cost:
- Model selection: using a smaller, fit-for-purpose model for routing (e.g., instruction-tuned 7B) for classification/intent can cut generation tokens by ~30% vs using a single 70B model for everything.
- Batching & concurrency: Redwood's continuous batching reduces per-token compute overhead; typical wins are 15-35% depending on request size and arrival patterns.
- KV/prefix caching: for chat-style flows with repeated system prompts or similar prefixes, KV caching can eliminate up to 60-70% of repeated compute for those tokens.
- Quantization & compilation: int8/4-bit model profiles give memory savings that allow cheaper GPU classes in Dedicated or Private, reducing infra cost ~20-30% depending on model.

Ballpark token economics (example for sizing):
- Baseline (current vendor): ~ $0.00012 per token (combined input+output) => 1,000,000 tokens ≈ $120
- Redwood hosted optimized (batching + model mix): expected ~ $0.00008-0.00010 per token => 1,000,000 tokens ≈ $80-$100
- With caching-on-chat-heavy flows: effective token bill for repeated prefixes can drop another 30-60% on those token classes.

Recommended next steps (proposed timeline):
1) I'll send an initial TCO workbook (attached) with a few usage scenarios (chat-heavy, generate-heavy, mixed). Please confirm which scenario best matches your plan. (Attachment: Acme_TCO_model_v1.xlsx)
2) Schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/ML infra folks and our Solutions Engineer to validate latency SLAs and discuss private deployment options. Proposed times: Thu 6/24 or Mon 6/28.
3) If helpful, we'll run a 2-week pilot on a subset of traffic (with evaluation credits) to produce concrete cost and latency numbers for your workload.

Attachments: Redwood_TCO_onepager.pdf (high-level framing), Acme_TCO_model_v1.xlsx (workbook), Redwood_token_econ_example.csv (example calculations).

Action items for Acme: confirm which usage scenario to populate and whether procurement needs any specific format for the TCO.

Thanks — happy to iterate quickly.

Best,
Rafael
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme TCO recap & next steps

Rafael,

Appreciate the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifying questions before we dig into the workbook: 

1) Can you provide a simple example of cost per 1M tokens for both hosted and dedicated (ballpark) with the model split you suggested? Procurement is specifically asking for a hosted vs reserved capacity delta.
2) For caching: do you have typical hit-rate assumptions you use for chat apps? Our main workflows have a lot of repeated system+prompt text across sessions.
3) Security: procurement wanted to confirm whether audit logs and regional VPC deployment are available for a pilot. If yes, they want a short checklist to include with the purchase request.

We're constrained by a Q3 budget cap for this initiative — procurement is trying to keep first-year spend under $180k. Can you indicate a likely path to ROI (savings or value) if we moved to Redwood vs our current setup?

I'm looping procurement here for transparency. We'd like the 45-min technical session; Thu 6/24 at 10:00 PT works for both of us if that slot is available on your side.

Thanks,
John
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme TCO recap & next steps

John,

Great questions. Short answers here and we'll expand in the workbook and on the call.

1) Example 1M-token math (ballpark):
- Hosted (mixed model strategy + batching): $0.00009 per token => 1M tokens ≈ $90.
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs, amortized infra + license): equivalent run-rate for steady 24/7 throughput can get to ~$0.00005-0.00007 per token => 1M tokens ≈ $50-$70 (note: depends on commitment length and utilization).

2) Caching assumptions: for chat flows with repeated system prompts + common user intents we see cache hit rates of 20-50% on average in early pilots; for very templated flows (support bots, transactional prompts) hit rates can exceed 60-70%. We'll model a conservative 30% hit rate in the workbook and show sensitivity to 10/30/60%.

3) Security & pilot checklist: yes — Redwood supports regionally isolated Private deployments, KMS integrations, and audit/event logs suitable for procurement review. I'll attach a short checklist and SOC2 summary on the call.

ROI framing (high level):
- For you: the most realistic near-term ROI will come from moving non-sensitive inference to optimized hosted + batching and routing to smaller models for routing/classification. With a Q3 spend cap of $180k, we'll show a scenario where you get to parity on feature quality while reducing per-token spend ~20-30% vs your current vendor — freeing budget for higher-value use cases.

Next: Thu 6/24 at 10:00 PT confirmed. I'll attach a one-pager with the token example and the workbook we discussed; Marissa (cc'd) will run point on the demo/SE staffing.
